record.paper_title: Weakly Picard operators: equivalent definitions, applications and open problems
record.context_brief: Converse fixed point principle for a unique periodic fixed point
record.original_question: Let X be a nonempty set and let A:X->X be an operator. Write A^0 for the identity on X and A^{n+1}=A composed with A^n, and write F_A={x in X: A(x)=x} for the fixed point set. Suppose there is a point x* in X such that F_A=F_{A^n}={x*} for every n>=1. Construct a K-metric d:X x X->K on X, meaning a K-valued distance with d(x,y)=0 iff x=y, d(x,y)=d(y,x), and d(x,z)<=d(x,y)+d(y,z), such that A becomes a contraction on (X,d). In the K-metric contraction formulation used in the same setting, this can be targeted by finding a positive linear operator Q:K->K with ||Q||<1 and d(Ax,Ay)<=Q(d(x,y)) for all x,y in X.

evidence.quote: FA = FAn = {x∗ }, for each n ∈ N∗ . Construct a K-metric d on X such that A : (X, d) → (X, d) is a contraction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a nonempty set and let $A:X\to X$ be an operator. Define $A^0=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $A^{n+1}=A\circ A^n$ for $n\ge 0$, and let $F_A=\{x\in X : A(x)=x\}$ denote the fixed point set of $A$. Assume there exists $x^*\in X$ such that
\[ F_A = F_{A^n} = \{x^*\} \qquad \text{for every } n\in\mathbb{N},\ n\ge 1. \]

Let $K$ be an ordered Banach space with positive cone, and call a map $d:X\times X\to K$ a $K$-metric on $X$ if for all $x,y,z\in X$:
(i) $d(x,y)\ge 0$ and $d(x,y)=0$ iff $x=y$;
(ii) $d(x,y)=d(y,x)$;
(iii) $d(x,z)\le d(x,y)+d(y,z)$.

The operator $A$ is called a $K$-metric contraction on $(X,d)$ if there exists a positive linear operator $Q:K\to K$ with $\lVert Q\rVert<1$ such that
\[ d(A(x),A(y))\le Q\bigl(d(x,y)\bigr) \qquad \text{for all } x,y\in X. \]

Problem: Construct an ordered Banach space $K$ and a $K$-metric $d$ on $X$ such that $A:(X,d)\to (X,d)$ is a $K$-metric contraction in the sense above.
artifact.status_search_result: This is listed as one of the open problems posed by I. A. Rus regarding converse statements of the contraction principle in the K-metric (generalized metric) setting. While classical scalar-metric converses to the Banach contraction principle are known (Bessaga-type theorems give a complete metric making each iterate a contraction whenever all iterates have a unique common fixed point), the corresponding K-metric/positive-linear-operator formulation is stated as an open construction problem and no published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Weakly Picard operators: Equivalent definitions, applications and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on weakly Picard operators including converse K-metric contraction constructions.
status_evidence.claim: The K-metric converse construction is posed as an open problem in the weakly Picard operators framework.

status_evidence.title: The Contraction Mapping Theorem (K. Conrad)
status_evidence.snippet: If each iterate f^n has a unique fixed point then there is a metric on X making f a contraction.
status_evidence.claim: A scalar-metric converse to the Banach contraction principle is known, but the K-metric version requires a positive linear operator Q with ||Q||<1.
